question.text: Under the SEBI AML Master Circular, which of the following best describes the concept of 'beneficial owner'?

answer.text: The person whose name appears on the account opening form
The broker or intermediary who manages the client's account
The natural person or persons who ultimately own, control or influence a client and/or the person on whose behalf a transaction is being conducted
Any nominee designated by the account holder

explanation.text: The Logic: The Series III-A workbook (pages 165-166) defines the beneficial owner as the natural person or persons who ultimately own, control or influence a client and/or the person on whose behalf a transaction is being conducted. The definition also captures those persons who exercise ultimate effective control over a legal person or arrangement. The Trap: Option A confuses the account holder with the beneficial owner. The two may differ — for example, where trusts, companies or nominee arrangements are used, the name on the account opening form is not necessarily the natural person who ultimately owns or controls the client. Note: Customer due diligence under the SEBI AML framework requires intermediaries to identify the beneficial owner and to understand the ownership and control structure of the client.
